title: Labubu’s Den
items: A new name, with Labubu as the icon.
Its own address on GitHub, so the link stays the same from now on.
Easier reading: no more text in capitals, and the introduction is set like the first page of a book.
An opening animation: a shooting star falls and lands on the title. Tap to skip it, or turn it off at the bottom of the page.
This update log. When new questions come in, the question count at the top of the homepage shows how many are new since your last visit.

title: Respiratory midterm quest
items: Every past exam question on the six midterm topics in one quest on the homepage: acute bronchitis, community-acquired pneumonia, pulmonary abscess, viral pneumonia, nosocomial pneumonia and bronchiectasis (60 questions).
A countdown to Wednesday 7 October, practice by topic, and your progress as you go.
Two seals to earn: answer them all with 80% right (retries count), or get 80% right on the first try.

title: The night sky
items: A new look: charcoal paper, bone ink and constellations.
Each module is an arched window holding its own constellation, and the stars light up as you get its questions right.
Smooth transitions between pages and between questions.

title: Topic search and the most repeated questions
items: Search by topic, not just by word: “acute bronchitis” finds every related question, even the ones that never say it. French terms, abbreviations (BPCO, IDM, RGO) and typos work too.
Narrow a search down to what the question asks about: signs, diagnosis, treatment, causes, complications.
Most repeated: the 224 questions that came up in two or more exam sets, ranked, with all their versions to practice.
Every question shows how many sets it was asked in, and each module has a Repeated only button.

title: The rest of S5
items: Mocks, finals, a second session and the professors’ question sets for every module.

title: The bank opens
items: The 2025–2026 midterms, sorted by module and by exam.
Tick every answer you think is right, then check it.
Each answer says where it comes from: the official key, the answers proposed in the doc, or a suggested answer with its reason when nothing was highlighted.
Notes and explanations from the docs under each question, with figures you can enlarge.
Your answers stay saved on your device: pick up where you left off, retry your mistakes, shuffle, or reset a module.
